atoms.definition: reset_n is an active-low asynchronous reset: queue occupancy is cleared to 0, in-flight requests and read returns are canceled, za_valid/data=0, command 1111, address/bank/mask=0, DQ is high-impedance, and cke is constantly 1. External memory contents are not cleared; read and write operations must remain inactive while reset is low.
atoms.timing: Assertion between edges takes effect immediately; after deassertion, the complete initialization sequence is performed again.
atoms.boundary: Reset during initialization, queuing, commands, or the read pipeline cancels them all; non-reset data registers are valid only after legal preparation.

atoms.definition: One entry is accepted on each rising edge when (!az_wr_n or !az_rd_n) and waitrequest=0 before the edge; az_cs does not gate acceptance, and acceptance is also allowed during initialization/refresh. Both operations low simultaneously encode a write. waitrequest indicates only that the two-entry FIFO is full; when full, no new entry is accepted even if a dequeue occurs on the same edge. When full, the source holds its request until it is accepted.
atoms.timing: Acceptance is determined by the full flag before the edge; enqueuing does not mean that SDRAM has completed the operation, and there is no combinational bypass for an empty queue.
atoms.boundary: Continuously asserted valid requests are accepted on every non-full edge; empty/one-entry/two-entry states, dequeue while full, different az_cs values, and simultaneous operations are all defined.

atoms.definition: The edge after the main controller fetches the first entry outputs ACT0011, the next edge outputs NOP, and the next edge outputs the first READ0101 or WRITE0100. The corresponding data is driven during a write command; at all other times, the bus is high-impedance. For the same direction/bank/row, column commands can be consecutive on every edge; after the prefetched tail entry is consumed, the final entry must not be issued again.
atoms.timing: The interval from enqueue to fetch is affected by initialization, the queue, refresh, and preceding entries, so there is no fixed total latency; use the main fetch edge or an observable ACT as the timing anchor.
atoms.boundary: Single entry, two entries, continuous streams, and queue-tail draining; DQ is driven only when write enable is active, read returns are provided externally, and bus contention is prohibited.

atoms.timing: An empty queue does not initiate precharge on its own; a new matching request performs a column access on the edge after it is fetched.

atoms.definition: After the startup count of 5000, refresh becomes due steadily once every 782 edges; the first operational refresh request is generated on edge 5783 after deassertion and remains asserted until serviced.
